summary: Rudolf Lange worked in Japanology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1923), teaching Berthold Laufer and Otto Rosenberg.

Rudolf Much was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1883–1887), where he later held a post from ~1895 to 1934 and taught Otto Höfler and Julius Pokorny.

Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, Rudolf Otto studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1888–1891) and under Richard von Garbe. He held positions at the University of Breslau (~1914–1917) and the University of Marburg (~1917–1929).
Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1852–1856) and later held an academic post there from ~1860 to 1892.

Linguist Rudolf Thurneysen studied at the University of Leipzig (~1877–1879) and under Heinrich Zimmer (~1879–1880). He held posts at the University of Jena (~1882–1887), University of Freiburg (~1887–1913), and University of Bonn (~1913–1923).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Evangelisches Stift Tübingen (~1839–1843) under Heinrich Ewald, and under Eugène Burnouf (~1843–1844). He held posts at the University of Tübingen starting in 1845 and from 1848 to 1895.

Indologist Rudrapatna Shamasastry studied at Government Sanskrit College, Mysore, the University of Madras (~1885–1889), Oriental University, and the University of Calcutta. He was Principal at Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala (1912–1918) and Curator at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (1918–1929).

Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen completed a PhD at Leiden University under Paul Harrison, also studying under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and is attested as faculty at Peking University in 2026.

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and served on the faculty at Yale University from ~1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BA (~1976–1980) and PhD (~1981–1987) under Lance S. Cousins at the University of Manchester, and held positions at the University of Bristol beginning in 1987.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, Ruriko Sakuma studied at Nagoya University. Sakuma has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Chicago (1927–1929) and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki and Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America (~1945–1967) and abbess of Ryōsen-an (~1958–1967).

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the Australian National University under John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman, later holding posts as a research associate there and as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2016).

Ruth Kempson is a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. She studied at the University of Birmingham (~1962–1966) and SOAS University of London (~1969–1973), and held an academic post at King's College London from ~1988 to 2010.
Ryan Anningson works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the supervision of Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Richard Overbey specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Brown University and Harvard University, later holding posts at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013–2015), and Wesleyan University (attested 2016).
Ryo Nishimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1995) and under Fumihiko Sueki (~1996–2004).
Ryodo Kudo works in Buddhist studies. Academic appointments include posts at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryoen Minamoto worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1948–1952), he held posts at Japan Women's University (~1964–1972), International Christian University (~1984–1989), and Tohoku University (~1984–2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1928–1932) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1939–1942). He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1940–1942) and held a professorship at Ryukoku University (~1952–1978).
